precepts.text: The Lord stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabians.
precepts.point: Tyre, Sidon and the coasts of Palestine, the Hamites, together with the Arabs, sold Israel to the Grecians. Records call slavery the result of raids by Arabs and Hamites on Negro communities.

precepts.why:
Joel says the nations “have scattered among the nations, and parted my land”, “cast lots for my people”, and he names who: “O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine”. The Zidonians are Canaanites, Hamites, and the coasts of Palestine are the Arabs. “The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.” This is nothing new. They did it before, in the days of an evil king named Jehoram.

Jehoram “walked in the way of the kings of Israel”, and in his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah and made themselves a king, “because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers.” Because of Jehoram’s disobedience and wickedness, God raised up enemies against him.

“Moreover the Lord stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians, that were near the Ethiopians”. The Philistines: that is Tyre and Zidon, the Hamites. And the Arabians, near the other Hamites. “And they came up into Judah, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king’s house, and his sons also, and his wives; so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.”

So the Hamites and the Arabs got together and stole his wives and his kids. It is their common nature to do that: they steal people. That is the same pair Joel names, and the records say it plainly: slavery in Africa was due to raids of Arabs and Hamites on Negro communities. The Hamite, the Arab and the white man worked together removing us far from our border, and the land is parted today between the Israelis and the Arabs. That is why God will plead with the nations in the valley of Jehoshaphat for his people.

precepts.text: Isaac's blessing to Esau, that he would serve his brother but break his yoke off his neck when he had the dominion, fulfilled here when Edom revolted.
precepts.point: Dealing with other gods is spiritual fornication, but physical fornication is built into these false worships; the pagan holidays passed down to our people, whatever the season, are built on fornication, and that is what draws the people to follow them.
precepts.why:
Isaac's blessing to Esau: “by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.”

It is fulfilled here: “In his days the Edomites revolted from under the dominion of Judah, and made themselves a king.” “So the Edomites revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day.” Libnah revolted at the same time, “because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers.”

When we obey the Most High the nations are subject to us; when we come out from under the commandments, that is when the other nations rise up and revolt against us and keep us in sin. Jehoram “made high places in the mountains of Judah, and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication, and compelled Judah thereto.” Dealing with other gods is spiritual fornication, but physical fornication is built into these false worships; the pagan holidays passed down to our people, whatever the season, are built on fornication, and that is what draws the people to follow them.

precepts.text: Every sickness not written in the book of the law the Most High would bring upon a disobedient people until they be destroyed.
precepts.point: His own body would be struck: he would have great sickness by disease of his bowels, until his bowels fell out by reason of the sickness day by day. This is what it looks like to mess with the Most High.
precepts.why:
“Also every sickness, and every plague, which is not written in the book of this law, them will the Lord bring upon thee, until thou be destroyed.”

That is what came on Jehoram. Elijah's writing charged him with walking “in the way of the kings of Israel”, making Judah and Jerusalem “to go a whoring, like to the whoredoms of the house of Ahab”, and slaying his brethren “which were better than thyself.” So: “with a great plague will the Lord smite thy people, and thy children, and thy wives, and all thy goods.”

And his own body was struck: “thou shalt have great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day.” This is what it looks like to mess with the Most High.

precepts.text: Because of disobedience many are weak and sickly, and many sleep, showing that sickness follows coming out from under the commandments.
precepts.point: His own body would be struck: he would have great sickness by disease of his bowels, until his bowels fell out by reason of the sickness day by day. This is what it looks like to mess with the Most High.
precepts.why:
“For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep.”

Because of disobedience many are weak and sickly, and many sleep. Sickness follows coming out from under the commandments. Jehoram had not walked “in the ways of Jehoshaphat thy father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah”, and the word to him was “great sickness by disease of thy bowels.”

points: Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.
Jehoshaphat had given his sons great gifts of silver, gold, and precious things with fenced cities, but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn.
As soon as Jehoram was risen up and strengthened himself, he slew all his brethren with the sword, along with divers of the princes of Israel.
Jehoram was thirty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab, meaning he was wicked; Israel's kings were all wicked, and he had the daughter of Ahab to wife.
Yet the Most High would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant He had made with David, promising to give a light to him and to his sons forever.

The Most High keeps His promises. Just as He did not break His word to David, He did not break His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; those promises were made to the Israelites and stand to this day, and we have plenty of proof of it.
In Jehoram's days Edom revolted from under the dominion of Judah and made themselves a king, and Libnah revolted at the same time because he had forsaken the Most High.
When we obey the Most High the nations are subject to us; when we come out from under the commandments, that is when the other nations rise up and revolt against us and keep us in sin.
Jehoram made high places in the mountains of Judah and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication and compelled Judah thereto.

There came a writing to Jehoram from Elijah the prophet, telling him he had not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat his father nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah, but in the way of the kings of Israel.
Elijah charged him with making Judah and Jerusalem go a whoring like the whoredoms of the house of Ahab, and with slaying his brethren who were better than himself.
The Most High declared He would smite his people, his children, his wives, and his goods with a great plague.

His own body would be struck: he would have great sickness by disease of his bowels, until his bowels fell out by reason of the sickness day by day. This is what it looks like to mess with the Most High.
Because of his disobedience his whole family was carried into captivity by the Philistines, the Arabs, and the Ethiopians, the same peoples who later held our people in the trans-Saharan slave trade.

The Most High stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabians that were near the Ethiopians, and they came up into Judah and carried away all his substance, his sons, and his wives, leaving only Jehoahaz his youngest.
After all this the Most High smote him in his bowels with an incurable disease, and at the end of two years his bowels fell out and he died of sore diseases.
He reigned eight years and departed without being desired; many were glad to see him go. They made no burning for him and buried him in the city of David but not in the sepulchres of the kings.
